key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINN formulations for semilinear parabolic Dirichlet boundary control and provides a conditional error analysis for the indirect approach.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a principled way to train PINNs for PDE-constrained control problems while estimating how approximation, optimization, quadrature, and soft-constraint errors affect solution quality.
method: Direct PINN: separate state and control networks minimize a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: joint networks for state, adjoint, and control enforce the optimality system with soft penalties for coupling and terminal/boundary constraints.
Derive linearized stability and residual-to-error estimates plus a computable residual indicator with conditional reliability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on two manufactured test problems, including a cubic reaction-diffusion equation and a linear benchmark with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint.
watch_item: The error guarantees are conditional on regularity, compatibility, neighborhood assumptions, and controlled soft-constraint residuals, so practical reliability may degrade if training leaves that regime.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
